# Factorial HR MCP connector

Manage company HR data with Factorial: inspect employees, organizational teams, leave requests, and attendance shifts. The AnythingMCP connector gives Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Cursor and Gemini 5 MCP tools for Factorial HR, all read-only.

[![Open Factorial HR in AnythingMCP Cloud](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20in-AnythingMCP%20Cloud-1f6feb?style=for-the-badge)](https://cloud.anythingmcp.com/login?mode=register&redirect=%2Fconnectors%2Fstore%3Finstall%3Dfactorial-hr&utm_source=github&utm_medium=catalog&utm_campaign=factorial-hr)

**Category:** [HR](../hr.md) · **Tools:** 5 · **Setup guide:** [anythingmcp.com](https://anythingmcp.com/marketplace/factorial-hr)

## Start without code

No installation and no terminal: AnythingMCP Cloud runs the Factorial HR connector for you, operated by helpcode.ai in Frankfurt, Germany.

1. **Click the button above** and create an account or sign in. The Factorial HR connector opens, ready to install.
2. **Paste the API key or token from your Factorial HR account.** Every click is in the [step-by-step guide](https://anythingmcp.com/marketplace/factorial-hr).
3. **Click Install.** AnythingMCP shows the address of your MCP server.
4. **Add that address to your assistant:** see the [guide](https://anythingmcp.com/marketplace/factorial-hr).
5. **Ask your first question.**

Prefer help with the setup? [Talk to us](https://anythingmcp.com/contact).

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  client["Claude · ChatGPT · Copilot · Cursor"]
  amcp["AnythingMCP<br/>roles · audit log · encrypted credentials"]
  api["Factorial HR API<br/>api.factorialhr.com"]
  client -- "MCP, OAuth or API key" --> amcp
  amcp -- "HTTPS, an API key" --> api
```

- **The AI client** speaks MCP (Streamable HTTP) to AnythingMCP and only sees tool names, descriptions and results. It never gets the Factorial HR credentials.
- **AnythingMCP** checks the client's role, builds the call from the tool definition, adds the credentials (an API key), calls Factorial HR, logs the call and returns the result.
- **Factorial HR** sees an ordinary API client with the rights of the account the credentials belong to.

## Tool reference

Every parameter as the AI client sees it in `tools/list`. Source: [`packages/backend/src/adapters/intl/factorial-hr.json`](../../../packages/backend/src/adapters/intl/factorial-hr.json).

### `factorial_hr_list_employees`

List company employees with directory details, contact information, role, and active status. Filter by name, email, team, manager status, or active employment. Paginate with after_id = meta.end_cursor while meta.has_next_page is true. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /api/2026-10-01/resources/employees/employees`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | no | Number of employees to return per page (default 20, maximum 100). |
| `after_id` | string | no | Cursor pointer to fetch records after this cursor (pass meta.end_cursor from previous page). |
| `before_id` | string | no | Cursor pointer to fetch records before this cursor (pass meta.start_cursor from previous page). |
| `only_active` | boolean | no | Set to true to return only active employees not terminated as of today. |
| `only_managers` | boolean | no | Set to true to return only employees who have at least one direct report. |
| `full_text_name` | string | no | Filter employees by searching for full or partial name. |
| `name_starts_with` | string | no | Filter employees whose first or last name starts with the given prefix. |
| `ids` | string[] | no | Filter employees by one or more specific employee IDs. |
| `emails` | string[] | no | Filter employees by one or more email addresses. |
| `team_ids` | string[] | no | Filter employees by one or more team IDs they belong to. |

### `factorial_hr_get_employee`

Retrieve detailed profile, personal information, contract details, and role for a single employee by their ID. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /api/2026-10-01/resources/employees/employees/{id}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The unique identifier of the employee to retrieve. |

### `factorial_hr_list_teams`

List company teams, departments, and organizational units with leader and parent team hierarchy. Filter by team IDs. Paginate with after_id = meta.end_cursor while meta.has_next_page is true. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /api/2026-10-01/resources/teams/teams`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | no | Number of teams to return per page (default 20, maximum 100). |
| `after_id` | string | no | Cursor pointer to fetch records after this cursor (pass meta.end_cursor from previous page). |
| `before_id` | string | no | Cursor pointer to fetch records before this cursor (pass meta.start_cursor from previous page). |
| `ids` | string[] | no | Filter by one or more specific team IDs. |

### `factorial_hr_list_leaves`

List employee time-off and leave requests with approval status, date ranges, and leave type. Set include_duration to request duration details and include_duration_by_day for the per-day breakdown (detailed fields are only populated when the corresponding option is requested). Filter by employee IDs, date window, or approval. Paginate with after_id = meta.end_cursor while meta.has_next_page is true. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /api/2026-10-01/resources/timeoff/leaves`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | no | Number of leave records to return per page (default 20, maximum 100). |
| `after_id` | string | no | Cursor pointer to fetch records after this cursor (pass meta.end_cursor from previous page). |
| `before_id` | string | no | Cursor pointer to fetch records before this cursor (pass meta.start_cursor from previous page). |
| `employee_ids` | string[] | no | Filter leaves by one or more employee IDs. |
| `ids` | string[] | no | Filter leaves by one or more specific leave IDs. |
| `from` | string | no | Filter leaves starting on or after this date (format YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `to` | string | no | Filter leaves ending on or before this date (format YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `approved` | boolean | no | Filter leaves by approval status (true for approved, false for unapproved/pending). |
| `only_active` | boolean | no | Set to true to exclude leaves belonging to terminated employees. |
| `include_deleted_leaves` | boolean | no | Whether to include deleted leaves (not included by default if not specified). |
| `include_duration` | boolean | no | Set to true to request duration information (duration_attributes, days_taken, hours_amount_in_cents). Detailed fields are only populated when requested. |
| `include_duration_by_day` | boolean | no | Set to true to request the per-day duration breakdown (duration_by_day_attributes). Detailed fields are only populated when requested. |

### `factorial_hr_list_shifts`

List employee attendance clock-in and clock-out shifts with recorded hours and locations. Filter by employee IDs or date window. Paginate with after_id = meta.end_cursor while meta.has_next_page is true. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /api/2026-10-01/resources/attendance/shifts`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | no | Number of shift records to return per page (default 20, maximum 100). |
| `after_id` | string | no | Cursor pointer to fetch records after this cursor (pass meta.end_cursor from previous page). |
| `before_id` | string | no | Cursor pointer to fetch records before this cursor (pass meta.start_cursor from previous page). |
| `employee_ids` | string[] | no | Filter attendance shifts by one or more employee IDs. |
| `ids` | string[] | no | Filter attendance shifts by one or more specific shift IDs. |
| `start_on` | string | no | Filter shifts starting on or after this date (format YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `end_on` | string | no | Filter shifts ending on or before this date (format YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `half_day` | boolean | no | Set to true to return only the shifts marked as covering half a day. Passing false has no effect. |
| `sort_created_at_asc` | boolean | no | Flag to sort attendance shifts by created_at in ascending order (default true). |

## Run it yourself

AnythingMCP is open source (AGPL-3.0). [Run it with Docker](../../../README.md#run-it-yourself), open **Connectors → Store**, pick **Factorial HR** and enter `FACTORIAL_API_KEY`, then add your MCP server URL to the AI client.
